post_title: Notches attached to segment points not grading properly on armhole
post_details: Hi, I have a couple of notch/segment point grading issues: 1. I've graded a bodice block and added two segment points with notches, the first point is 2" away from side seam, the other is 1" away from that point. These measurements are inconsistent throughout the graded sizes, how can I quickly ensure all segment points are the same measurements away from the side seam? 2. I notice that when I add segment points onto the graded armhole, the curves becomes warped (see the before and after pics). How can I keep the graded curves consistent? Thank you.

comments.comment_body: Dear 10631114586521, What version of CLO are you using?
Version 7.1
10631114586521 Are you currently using a CLO license under a different account name? We see no current license with your user name.
Yes I am, sorry for the confusion! I am using the account under User ID firststop
Commenting here.

18871009185561 and 10631114586521 Thank you so much for clarifying :) 1) When you grade out Segments grade from one point to the next. So you cannot "lock" a Segment point a certain amount/distance when grading. (You can technically choose to grade a Segment Line instead of a Point, but we do NOT recommend this). Instead it would be better to convert the Segment points to Curve Points and then use the Notch Tool on the 2D Tool Bar. Once you apply the notch you can select it with the Notch Tool and go to the Property Editor &gt You will see an option to Lock. Check this on and then choose from Start or End Point. 2) It is best to not add additional Segment Points once you have added grading. You want to make sure that the pattern is complete and then Move to grading
This is exactly what I needed, thank you!!
Hi 18871009185561 Wonderful! We are so happy we could help!!!

post_title: Have big gap when use Layer Clone Over
post_details: Hi When I use Layer Clone Over feature, they will make the big gap as below: Then I need to delete sewing then sew again: It will cost the time if I sew again and again. What should I do? Thank Travis

comments.comment_body: Hello 903004757723 Have a look at the attached image. I did the following Reduced the Collision Thickness between all the pattern pieces. Selected the Layer Clone Layers with Edit Sewing and applied TURNED for the Sewing Line Type Selected ALL sewing and removed intensity of the 3D Sewing effect Changed the Physical Properties of Fabric 1 to match Leather Lambskin so they would have the same thickness. Selected all layers and removed Curved Side Geometry Turned off the Seamlines in the garment options in the 3D toggle menu Removed all Pressure Used Fitting Simulation Because you have Layer Clones, which are sewn to the under layer, you will not get flat/smooth connections. IF you physically had one entire layer of the whole thing inside the other, you could get smooth seams. Hope this helps... All the Best, Jim Simon, Specialist, 3D Design &amp Implementation

post_title: Hide lower body? Want torso only, thighs still visible
post_details: Is it possible to add another cut to divide the body of the avatar so I can only show the neck, head and arms of the avatar? I can turn off the opacity of the legs but I don't want the thighs visible either.

comments.comment_body: Dear 16606310914201, CLO avatars are divided into legs, arms, torso (with start of thigh as is common in fashion half mannequins), and head region (this one has a few more separate components). Hiding pieces of the avatar is directly linked to these divisions, so unfortunately, it is currently not possible to hide this part of the thigh without hiding the rest of the torso. A workaround going for a final render would be to render twice, once with and once without avatar, and merging the images together. We will add your comment as a feature request.

post_details: hi, when making garments am i supposed to make my final designs off of the basic patterns i make in clo3d. or am i supposed to make the final designs based off the model. and how does seam allowance work? any suggestions would help. thank you.

comments.comment_body: Dear 17121374128025, you can create garments in whichever way you wish. If you do not have access to other patterns, you can use the blocks in the Modular Configurator (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=xNoY_aIeWMM) as starting points, or you can use the 3D Pen (Avatar) to mold pattern pieces from the avatar's form (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6nKllTXUtP0). You can also create block patterns from scratch (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MXZeSqCOi1Q). The active pattern outline is without seam allowance, so what you are seeing is the actual sewing outline. If you wish to add seam allowance to your patterns, please use the seam allowance tool: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ymzkFaceBek&ampt=492s
Thank You
